proposal.direction: +1 at index 0 only (steps 10-25): amplification of the highest-delivery guidance window; anchor [5,5,5,5] -> [6,5,5,5], 1 changed index, within 0-10 bounds and default +/-1 tick limit
proposal.exploration_degree: low-mass single-window amplitude probe on the dominant delivered window
proposal.hypothesis: Index 0 carries the largest delivered displacement (mean guidance_native_ratio 0.00765, max_atom_guidance_A 0.00094 A), so adding one tick there is the most likely single edit to produce a measurable paired Mean change; direction of that change is untested.
proposal.expected_mean_effect: Largest-magnitude Mean response among the four single-window probes, sign unknown; compared against the round-0 incumbent Mean 4.1724 (tool:1f67e4d9...). Concentrated rather than uniform response is likely.
proposal.expected_best_effect: Best change should be small vs 7.7081 because the added delivered displacement (~0.1 tick scale, tick_to_amplitude 0.1) is sub-0.001 A; a Best change would suggest the top candidates sit on a steep local response.
proposal.falsifier: If the paired Mean(B-A) for this arm is indistinguishable from the H2 reversal arm and its partner bracket, or if interval diagnostics show the delivered inside_rms_A at steps 10-25 does not increase at all, then the window-0 amplification premise is unsupported.
proposal.diagnostic_alternative: If Mean moves but Best is flat, interpretation shifts to a broad modest-response effect rather than top-candidate refinement; if neither moves, the delivered-control scale is too small at one tick to matter and later rounds should test two-index edits.
proposal.expected_subgroup_response: Any gain should concentrate in candidates whose baseline scores sit near Median 3.49 by shifting them upward; q90-top candidates near 6.78 are expected to be least responsive.
proposal.revision_from_previous_result: Bootstrap round: no prior executed arm exists, and latest-vs-incumbent is a self-identity (delta 0.0), so this is a first signed probe rather than a revision of a measured direction.

proposal.direction: -1 at index 0 only (steps 10-25): attenuation/reversal of the same window used by H1; anchor [5,5,5,5] -> [4,5,5,5], 1 changed index, bounds and +/-1 limit satisfied
proposal.exploration_degree: low-mass reversal partner forming a signed bracket with H1 at equal amplitude
proposal.hypothesis: Paired with H1, this separates the sign of the window-0 response: if plus is better than minus, index-0 guidance helps Mean; if both sit below a flat-guidance outcome, guidance there is not simply beneficial in this context.
proposal.expected_mean_effect: Mean(B-A) vs H1 with the same 100 identities should be opposite in sign to H1's own effect if a monotone slope exists on index 0; magnitude comparable to H1's, measured against Mean 4.1724.
proposal.expected_best_effect: Best expected near-flat relative to 7.7081; a drop in Best under reduced window-0 guidance would be the first evidence that retained top candidates depend on that window.
proposal.falsifier: If H1 and H2 produce statistically similar Mean shifts in the same direction, the response is not a simple slope on index 0 and amplification should not be escalated in later rounds.
proposal.diagnostic_alternative: A null on both arms with unchanged geometry would indicate the tick-to-displacement mapping is too coarse for index 0, favouring a later test that edits two indices at once.
proposal.expected_subgroup_response: Under attenuation, losses should fall on the q90-subgroup if its members depend most on early guidance; low-quartile candidates are expected to be least affected.
proposal.revision_from_previous_result: Bootstrap round: added because the only existing paired record (latest vs incumbent) is the same population compared with itself and cannot supply a direction.

proposal.direction: +1 at index 1 only (steps 26-50): amplification of the second guidance window; anchor [5,5,5,5] -> [5,6,5,5], 1 changed index, bounds and +/-1 limit satisfied
proposal.exploration_degree: low-mass single-window probe on a lower-delivery, mid-run window
proposal.hypothesis: Index 1 delivers about half the displacement of index 0 (guidance_native_ratio 0.00379, inside_rms_A 0.00042 A) but overlaps the only interval with any clipping (clipped_fraction 0.0004), so one tick here tests whether mid-run control matters out of proportion to its magnitude.
proposal.expected_mean_effect: Smaller Mean response than H1 in absolute value if effect scales with delivered displacement; compared against the round-0 Mean 4.1724.
proposal.expected_best_effect: Minimal change expected in Best 7.7081 and Top10 7.2422; a Best increase without a Mean increase would point to a narrow top-candidate effect.
proposal.falsifier: If this arm's paired Mean shift exceeds the H1 window-0 shift while its delivered displacement stays about half, the displacement-scaling assumption is wrong and window identity dominates.
proposal.diagnostic_alternative: If mean gradient_drift_cosine for steps 26-50 (-0.082) becomes less negative together with a Mean gain, drift sign is informative; if drift changes and Mean does not, drift is decorative rather than causal.
proposal.expected_subgroup_response: Response expected to be diffused across score quartiles rather than concentrated, since mid-run refinement affects most candidates mildly.
proposal.revision_from_previous_result: Bootstrap round: window 1 chosen for the second positive probe because it covers 25 steps, the widest single interval, giving the best chance of a detectable effect at one tick.

proposal.direction: +1 at index 3 only (steps 76-90): amplification of the short terminal guidance window; anchor [5,5,5,5] -> [5,5,5,6], 1 changed index, bounds and +/-1 limit satisfied
proposal.exploration_degree: low-mass probe distinguishing late-window control from early-window control
proposal.hypothesis: Steps 51-90 show the most negative mean gradient_drift_cosine (-0.153, -0.142) with low displacement, so a one-tick late increase tests whether late control helps Mean, is neutral, or reproduces the late negative-drift pattern.
proposal.expected_mean_effect: Small-to-null Mean effect vs 4.1724; this arm is as much diagnostic as gain-seeking, and a null result with unchanged geometry would be informative.
proposal.expected_best_effect: Best likely unchanged from 7.7081; a Best gain here would indicate final-state refinement matters more than early contact.
proposal.falsifier: If the paired Mean delta is null and interval diagnostics show no change in late displacement, clipping or switch fraction, then one tick in index 3 is below the resolution of this schedule and late-window escalation should not be pursued.
proposal.diagnostic_alternative: If late guidance increases Best while leaving Mean flat, the effect is top-candidate-specific; if it lowers Mean while raising late displacement, extra late motion is unhelpful in this context.
proposal.expected_subgroup_response: Any effect should concentrate in the q90 subgroup (scores near 6.78 and above) because late refinement can only adjust already-favourable conformations.
proposal.revision_from_previous_result: Bootstrap round: no earlier executed result exists; this arm is included so late-window response is measured in the same round as the early-window bracket rather than assumed from drift sign.

proposal.direction: Increase guidance amplitude in interval 0 (steps 10-25) from 0.5 to 0.6; intervals 1-3 unchanged at 0.5. One changed interval, +1 tick, inside bounds and the default one-tick limit.
proposal.exploration_degree: single-interval upward probe in the window with the highest delivered guidance ratio (0.0066) and zero clipping
proposal.hypothesis: The earliest guidance window delivers the most control (guidance_native_ratio 0.0066 vs 0.0017 at 51-75) and already shows a mild negative drift cosine (-0.035). If delivered early control is under-used rather than misdirected, +0.1 amplitude there should improve core convergence and lift the unselected Mean above the 4.069 incumbent baseline.
proposal.expected_mean_effect: Small positive versus incumbent Mean 4.069 if delivered early control is limiting; no more than a marginal shift is expected because only one interval and one tick change.
proposal.expected_best_effect: Neutral to slightly positive against Best 7.708; the upper tail (Top10 7.059) is already near the teacher, so a gain should not be expected mainly from Best.
proposal.falsifier: If paired Mean (H1 minus incumbent) is indistinguishable from zero and Best does not exceed 7.708, delivered early-guidance amplitude is not a lever and the early window should not be escalated further.
proposal.diagnostic_alternative: If Mean is flat but step-100 core RMS drops below the 2.015 Å baseline, that separates 'guidance amplitude affects geometry' from 'geometry change affects score'.
proposal.expected_subgroup_response: Quartiles fixed by the incumbent scores. If any gain appears, check whether it concentrates in the lower quartiles (which carry the Mean deficit at median 3.476) or only in the top quartile already at Top10 Mean 7.059; equal-looking extreme deltas do not identify the same candidate.
proposal.revision_from_previous_result: No prior executed result exists (latest equals incumbent), so this is a first direction-discovery arm, not a revision.

proposal.direction: Decrease guidance amplitude in interval 0 (steps 10-25) from 0.5 to 0.4; intervals 1-3 unchanged. One changed interval, -1 tick, within bounds and the one-tick limit.
proposal.exploration_degree: matched opposite-direction probe to H1 in the same window, providing a slope read
proposal.hypothesis: Paired with H1, this brackets the incumbent amplitude in the highest-guidance window. If the early delivered guidance is already stronger than useful (mild negative drift cosine -0.035) or is pulling core atoms off the productive path while unclipped, reducing it by 0.1 should raise the unselected Mean above 4.069 even though less control is delivered.
proposal.expected_mean_effect: Small positive versus incumbent if early guidance is over-driven; small negative if the delivered early control is genuinely helpful. Direction is the point of the arm.
proposal.expected_best_effect: Neutral to slightly negative for Best 7.708, since lower guidance is less likely to push the extreme tail upward.
proposal.falsifier: If H1 and H2 both sit at the incumbent Mean with no Best change, amplitude in the early window is not a lever in this context and escalation or reversal there should stop.
proposal.diagnostic_alternative: Together with H1 this is a three-point slope test (0.4 / 0.5 / 0.6) around the incumbent; a gain-then-loss pattern would discourage further increase in this window only.
proposal.expected_subgroup_response: Quartiles fixed by incumbent scores. A reduction in delivered control plausibly shifts candidates that currently sit near the median (3.476) more than the Top10 group; verify with a paired subgroup read rather than assuming.
proposal.revision_from_previous_result: No prior executed result exists; this arm exists only to make H1's direction interpretable.

proposal.direction: Increase guidance amplitude in interval 2 (steps 51-75) from 0.5 to 0.6; intervals 0, 1 and 3 unchanged. One changed interval, +1 tick, legal from anchor [5,5,5,5].
proposal.exploration_degree: single-interval upward probe in the window with the lowest delivered guidance ratio (0.0017) and the most negative drift cosine (-0.131)
proposal.hypothesis: Delivered control is weakest in 51-75 while drift opposes guidance and endpoint geometry is still ~2 Å from the native core. If that window is under-guided, +0.1 amplitude there should improve the final rescore of many middle candidates and raise the unselected Mean above 4.069 without relying on the already-high Top10 group.
proposal.expected_mean_effect: Small positive versus incumbent Mean 4.069 if mid-run under-guidance is limiting; small negative if the low delivered amplitude there is protective.
proposal.expected_best_effect: Neutral for Best 7.708; the median-to-q90 band (3.476 to 6.560) is the more likely place for a response.
proposal.falsifier: If paired Mean is flat and step-100 core RMS stays at the 2.015 Å baseline, the mid-window amplitude is not limiting and the remaining error should be treated as a direction problem rather than an amplitude problem.
proposal.diagnostic_alternative: If Mean moves but step-100 core RMS does not, the score response came through a route other than terminal core-atom geometry, which would redirect later arms away from geometry-targeted edits.
proposal.expected_subgroup_response: Quartiles fixed by incumbent scores; a mid-window edit is expected to move the middle bands, so a response confined to the top score quartile would argue against the under-guidance reading.
proposal.revision_from_previous_result: No prior executed result exists; window choice is driven by the baseline interval_diagnostics rather than any observed score response.

proposal.direction: Increase guidance amplitude in interval 3 (steps 76-90) from 0.5 to 0.6; intervals 0-2 unchanged. One changed interval, +1 tick, legal, and distinct from H1-H3.
proposal.exploration_degree: single-interval upward probe in the terminal guided window, before guidance switches off at step 91
proposal.hypothesis: The most negative drift cosine (-0.148) occurs in 76-90, guidance ratio there (0.0030) is stronger than at 51-75, and guidance stops entirely after step 90, after which drift turns positive. If the last guided window is where remaining geometry error could still be corrected cheaply, +0.1 amplitude there should lift terminal core convergence and the unselected Mean above 4.069.
proposal.expected_mean_effect: Small positive versus incumbent if the terminal guided window is the efficient place to spend extra control; otherwise flat.
proposal.expected_best_effect: Neutral to slightly positive for Best 7.708, since late control can affect where the final rescore lands for already-good candidates.
proposal.falsifier: If paired Mean is flat and the step-100 geometry distribution is unchanged from RMS 2.015 Å mean, terminal amplitude is not the binding constraint and the unguided tail (91-99, drift cosine +0.057) becomes the more plausible place to look.
proposal.diagnostic_alternative: A gain here without a 51-75 (H3) gain distinguishes terminal-only control from general mid/late under-guidance; both flat would point at the post-step-91 unguided phase.
proposal.expected_subgroup_response: Quartiles fixed by incumbent scores; late control could either help the upper band consolidate or help the median band catch up, so the subgroup read decides which of those two is claimed.
proposal.revision_from_previous_result: No prior executed result exists; this arm is included alongside H3 to separate terminal from mid-run effects within one round.
